nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that feed the bay's filter feeders and zooplankton. Too many nutrients cause blooms that block light and use up oxygen when they die and decay.

nodes.name: Underwater grasses
nodes.desc: Submerged grass beds that give food and shelter, add oxygen and clear the water. Eelgrass in the southern bay has shrunk by more than half since the early 1970s.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny animals that graze phytoplankton. Young menhaden and bay anchovies feed on them.

nodes.name: Atlantic menhaden
nodes.desc: A schooling filter feeder that strains plankton from the water. Striped bass, bluefish, ospreys, eagles and dolphins all eat it.

nodes.name: Bay anchovy
nodes.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is a key forage fish for larger fish and birds.

nodes.name: Eastern oyster
nodes.desc: A filter feeder that strains plankton from the water, clearing it as it feeds. Its reefs give hard surfaces and shelter to many other species.

nodes.name: Bottom clams & worms
nodes.desc: Seafloor dwellers that feed on plankton and detritus. Summer low-oxygen zones kill them, which removes a key food source for blue crabs.

nodes.name: Sea nettle
nodes.desc: A stinging jellyfish of the bay's summer waters that feeds on zooplankton.

nodes.name: Blue crab
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats clams, mussels, oysters, worms, small fish and eelgrass, and also scavenges. Striped bass are among its predators.

nodes.name: Diamondback terrapin
nodes.desc: A salt-marsh turtle that eats crabs, snails, clams, worms and fish. Raccoons are its main nest predator.

nodes.name: Striped bass
nodes.desc: The bay is one of the biggest breeding areas for this large predator, which eats menhaden, herring, shad and other fish.

nodes.name: Bluefish
nodes.desc: A fast schooling predator that hunts forage fish such as menhaden.

nodes.name: Bottlenose dolphin
nodes.desc: Visits the bay seasonally or year-round and eats fish including menhaden.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: A fish-eating hawk that plunges feet first to catch live fish, almost all of its diet. Menhaden are among its prey.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: A large raptor that eats fish and carrion along the bay. Its numbers recovered after the DDT era.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light drives growth of algae and underwater grasses, but algae and sediment can block it from reaching bottom plants.

nodes.name: Nutrient runoff
nodes.desc: Nitrogen and phosphorus from farms, towns, sewage and air pollution wash into the bay and fuel algal blooms.

nodes.name: Bottom-water oxygen
nodes.desc: In summer the layered water traps oxygen-poor water near the bottom, where dissolved oxygen can drop to near zero.

nodes.name: Bacteria & decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the water. Decaying blooms use up oxygen.
